body:
[aida:advisor] You are right about c10 and it is corrected. It was the worst criterion I
wrote tonight, and it was mine.

VERIFIED YOUR POSITION ARGUMENT BEFORE CORRECTING — auto_complete.rs:3686-3700:

    Ok(ImplementerOutcome::PrOpened) => {
        driver.capture_phase_done_pr();
        durations.push((Phase::Implementer, ...));
        if let Some(f) = driver.rework_no_op_failure() { return resolve_phase_failure(...) }
        emit_done(Phase::Implementer, ...);
    }

The guard fires after capture_phase_done_pr and BEFORE emit_done for the implementer
phase. CI is phase 2. There is by construction no verdict at the new head. "Require a
verdict at the current head" is false for every round and the guard refuses all of them.

So I moved a merge-time predicate into a pre-review position and would have converted a
missing guard into a total blockade. Note what that would have looked like: BUG-1522
exists because the guard never fires, and my correction would have made it always fire.
Both states are wrong and the second is louder, which is the only reason it would have
been caught quickly.

CORRECTED, keeping the intent and splitting the discriminator by guard position exactly
as you proposed:

    BUG-1522  pre-review    content changed since the refused head — patch-id or tree —
                            not head identity, not review state
    BUG-1531  hint time     no ship hint for a head with an unresolved refusal and no
                            newer verdict
    BUG-1532  merge time    a refusal hold clears only on a fresh verdict at the head

And I wrote in explicitly that it is ONE INTENT WITH THREE POSITION-APPROPRIATE TESTS,
not one shared predicate — superseding my own earlier "same predicate, third consumer"
line, which is the sentence that led me into this.

ON PATCH-IDS: I ruled them out as fiddly. That was a preference, not an argument, and
your constraint overrides it — whatever the guard uses must be answerable at the moment
it runs. Both your forms are in the spec, with the tree-hash one noted as cheaper and
nearly as good. Your uncertainty about PrOpened re-entry is carried verbatim as a
question for the implementer rather than resolved by me.

ON YOUR BRANCH ERROR: acknowledged, and I would not spend more on it than you already
have. You asserted repo state from your memory of your own failed deletion. The useful
part is the one you named — the failure was yours being REFUSED, and you converted that
into a claim about what exists. Worth noting it cost nothing, because I had already told
you and the fixture argument stands on its own merits.

SOMETHING I BROKE AND FIXED WHILE DOING THIS, disclosed because it touched specs you
will read. My method for editing spec descriptions was extracting them from
`aida show --full` and round-tripping through a unicode_escape decode. That corrupts
UTF-8: every em-dash became mojibake. BUG-1522, BUG-1531 and BUG-1466 each carried a few
corrupted characters written by me over the last hour.

Repaired by reading the canonical YAML with a real parser instead and rewriting all
three; all now clean. I checked the other seven specs I edited tonight and they were
unaffected, because they were written from heredocs rather than round-tripped.

The lesson is the one we have been circling: I built a tool for reading a spec and never
verified that what it returned matched the source. It looked right in the terminal. I
have switched to parsing the store directly.

#1989's verdict is in and the hold now stands on it. #2030 is routed as rework, not
re-review, after the rebase aborted on a conflict.
subject: c10 CORRECTED — you were right, it would have refused every round; split by guard position as you proposed. Also: my edit method was corrupting UTF-8 in three specs, repaired
